Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

malice noun

also spite, ill will, roguery, mischief

classical

Plaut. Aul. 215: tē cīvem sine malā omnī malitiā
Cic. Tusc. 4.34: nam malitia certī cujusdam vitiī nōmen est (Lewis & Short)

malitia, malitiae f.

noun, first declension

ill will, spite, malice; roguery

Cicero keeps it for one particular vice and says vitiōsitās for badness in general.

Examples

  • Certē edepol equidem tē cīvem sine malā omnī malitiā semper sum arbitrātus et nunc arbitror.

    Truly, I have always thought you a citizen without a trace of malice, and I think so still.Plaut. Aul. 215–216

See also cunning, evil, naughty.

SourcesLewis & Short: malitia

Plautus, Aulularia 215–216.
